caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 742 of 1997.
lawyer: Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record — For Petitioner.  Not Represented — Respondents.
parties:
Jane Alam Khan ------ Petitioner
VS.
Abdul Hamid Chowdhury and another ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This petition for leave to appeal is from the judgment and order dated 17-7-97 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1997 rejecting the petitioner's application under section 10A of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1981 for drawing up a proceeding for contempt against the two respondents. 

 2. The petitioner, a District Controller of Food, was placed under suspension on 26-1-92. He was proceeded against on a charge of misconduct and corruption under the provisions of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985, shortly the Rules, 1985 and was ultimately dismissed from service by an order dated 7-12-93 with a further direction for recovery from him of a sum of Taka 2,09,70,909.47. The petitioner filed Administrative Tribunal Case No. 409 of 1993 on 16-12-93 and by judgment and order dated 9-4-96 the Administrative Tribunal allowed the case on contest with the following direction: 

 "So much of the judgment and order dated 9-4-96 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka allowing AT Case No. 409 of 1993 as it relates to denying the petitioner-appellant's financial benefits for the period he was kept out of office beginning from the date of his suspension till the date of his joining on reinstatement, is set aside. The judgment and order minus as above is affirmed subject to addition that the petitioner-appellant is still in service and is entitled to be reinstated in service with attending benefits including arrear pay and allowances." 

 7. We have perused Rule 11(3) as amended upto date. It gives to the Government a discretion on consideration of the circumstances of the case to institute a fresh inquiry against a delinquent officer on the same cause of action if the earlier order of punishment was set aside by an Administrative Tribunal or by any other Court. The said Rule also provides that such a decision being taken the delinquent officer shall be deemed to be on suspension from the original date of dismissal. This is what the Government did by the impugned order dated 16-6-97 and it is not the case of the petitioner that the Government did not consider the facts of the case of the petitioner at all. When that is the states of the Rules framed under a constitutional provision it cannot be said that the respondents acted in willful and contemptuous disregard of the judgment and order of the Appellate Tribunal dated 27-5-97.
